name: Select
description: A dropdown for choosing one option from a list. It's the native select with a nicer list on desktop, and the system picker on touch devices.

classes.ayy-select: Wrapper element. Draws the chevron and sets the height.
classes.ayy-select__list: The options list (role="listbox" popover) that React Select and "@danitesler/ayywi/elements" build from the <option>s while it's open. Don't write it yourself.
classes.ayy-select__option: One option in the list (role="option"); aria-selected="true" on the chosen one, aria-disabled for a disabled <option>.
classes.ayy-select__picture: A picture for one option (a theme thumbnail, "Aa" in a font, a colour): a <span aria-hidden="true" data-value="<the option's value>"> after the <select> in the wrapper, one per option, all but the chosen one hidden. The chosen one shows at the control's inline start (32×20px); the list shows each before its option's text (88px wide, 16:10). It's a frame (border, tint, rounded) and a size container, so what's inside can size itself in container units.

default.looks: Native <select> with a wash fill, line-strong border and a muted chevron at the inline end.

hover.looks: Border turns line-hover; an option in the list gets the wash-hover background.

pressed.none: Pressing opens the options list (the OS picker on touch screens); the list shows the state.

focus.looks: 2px ring just inside the edge; the border goes transparent. In the list the focused option gets the wash-hover background, plus a 2px ring inset by 2px from the keyboard. Forced colours: Highlight fill.

disabled.when: .ayy-select__control:disabled; a disabled <option> (aria-disabled on its list option)
disabled.looks: Control and chevron dim to --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor; a disabled option dims the same way and the arrow keys skip it.

selected.looks: The chosen option shows as the control's text (and its picture, when the select has pictures); in the list it's semibold with a check at the inline end.

error.looks: Border 60% destructive, destructive focus ring. Forced colours: dashed border.

loading.none: No loading look; disable it with a "Loading…" option until the options arrive, or use a Skeleton for the form.

open.looks: Border turns line-hover and the chevron points up; the list fades in and scales up from 97% under the select (above it when there's no room), at least as wide, at most 20rem tall with its own scroll.

multiple.looks: Renders a list box: no fixed height, no chevron, no options list.

scale.sm: Control sm height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), sm text.
scale.md: Control md height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch).
scale.lg: Control lg height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), lg text.

sizes.width: Fills its container; long option text is cut with an ellipsis. The list is at least the select's width and at most 24rem; its options are the md control height, or as tall as their picture (up to 32rem of list) with pictures.

js: selectClass({ size?, className? }) → string for the wrapper; selectControlClass, selectListClass, selectOptionClass, selectLabelClass constants; openSelectListFrom(event) opens the list from a mousedown or keydown on a select (what React Select and "@danitesler/ayywi/elements" call); openSelectList(select) opens it directly; usesSelectList(select) says whether a select gets the list here; selectPictureClass, selectPicture(select, value) and syncSelectPicture(select) (shows the chosen option's picture; @danitesler/ayywi/elements calls it on change). Choosing from ayywi's list fires input and change when the value changes, then a bubbling ayy-choose event (detail.value) on the select for every choice, the option already chosen included

props.pictures: Record<string, ReactNode> — a picture per option value: rendered as .ayy-select__picture spans after the <select>; the chosen one shows before the text and the list shows each
props.onChoose: (value: string) => void — every choice from ayywi's list, the option already chosen included (onChange only fires for a new one), for an option that acts each time, such as Custom colour
props....rest: All native <select> attributes and events (onChange fires when an option is chosen from the list too); className goes to the <select>.

a11y: Label it like any input (Field + Label with for/id); the list takes the same name.
The list is a role="listbox" of role="option"s: arrows, Home/End and type-ahead move, Enter, Space or a click chooses, Esc, Tab or a click outside closes, and focus goes back to the select.
Touch screens keep the OS picker, which suits them better. Don't build your own dropdown for choosing a value: this is it.
Pictures are aria-hidden: an option's text names it, in the list and in the OS picker.
do: Use a select to choose one option from a longer list (country, time zone, role).
Put a sensible default first, or a disabled placeholder option.
Write a plain <select> with <option>s (or React Select): the list comes with it. In plain HTML load elements.global.js (or import "@danitesler/ayywi/elements").

Give options pictures when the choice is visual (a theme, a font, a colour): one .ayy-select__picture per option (React: pictures). Phones keep the OS picker with text only, so the option text must still say what it is.
dont: Don't use a select for 2–5 options that should all be visible — use Radio, or a Segmented control when the choice changes a view.
Don't use a select for actions — use a Dropdown menu.
Don't build a custom dropdown (a button opening a div of choices, a Dropdown menu used as a picker) — use Select, or a Combobox when people should type to filter.
Don't use a select to search thousands of options — put a search Input group above a List of results instead.
Don't use a select for yes/no — use a Switch or Checkbox.
